items.title: The first cultured meat burger
items.claim: The first publicly cooked and tasted cultured meat burger was presented in London in 2013. Roughly what did it cost to produce?
items.reveal_title: About a third of a million dollars per burger
items.reveal:
Mark Post's 5 August 2013 demonstration used cultured bovine muscle cells. The project was funded by Sergey Brin.

By 2023 Singapore and the US approved limited cultured chicken sales; production costs remain orders of magnitude above conventional meat.
items.why: Technologies start at extreme costs that fall steeply if scale is achieved.

items.title: The MSG 'syndrome' myth
items.claim: The idea that monosodium glutamate causes a distinctive 'Chinese restaurant syndrome' came from a 1968 letter to the New England Journal of Medicine. What does the controlled evidence show?

options.text: Robust evidence MSG causes the symptoms in most people
Double-blind trials have not consistently linked MSG within typical food levels to the reported symptoms
MSG is toxic at any dose

items.reveal_title: The popular reaction outran the evidence
items.reveal:
Reviews including the US Food and Drug Administration's classification of MSG as 'Generally Recognised As Safe' (GRAS) and double-blind challenge studies have not consistently reproduced the symptoms at dietary doses.

Kikunae Ikeda first isolated glutamate as the source of umami in 1908 at Tokyo Imperial University.
items.why: A high-profile anecdote can shape food policy and public perception for decades.

items.title: Coeliac disease prevalence
items.claim: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune reaction to gluten. What is the approximate population prevalence in Western countries based on serological screening?
items.reveal:
Singh et al. (2018, meta-analysis) reported a global pooled seroprevalence of 1.4% and biopsy-confirmed prevalence of 0.7%. Most cases remain undiagnosed.

Non-coeliac gluten sensitivity is a separate, less well-characterised category.
items.why: Population screening reveals that some conditions are far more common than clinic-based estimates suggest.
